label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: Please do not enter No. 43 or prop it

Mick — please do not go into No. 43 at 9, send your lad in, install props or inspect the loft from inside. Priya, please don’t provide a key for this. I know it’s well-meant, but it could put you both in a collapse zone.

I walked past at 7.05am. From the opposite pavement I could see roughly 1.2m of No. 41’s stack still standing, leaning towards No. 43, with visibly washed-out mortar at its base. No. 43’s front roof slope has a hole of about 2–3m². There is a stepped (stair-shaped) crack, roughly 5–10mm wide, from above the bay window up to the first-floor window sill. The top of the bay appears to have dropped about 20mm. There are also loose slates above the footway at both 43 and 45. Gusts around 50mph are forecast again this afternoon.

Standing beneath that holed roof, with the damaged stack above, is just about the worst place to put a prop. Fallen masonry may already be loading the ceilings and floors, and the impact damage means the load path — how the building’s weight is carried down safely — is now unknown. An acrow can transfer or add load to something already weakened. This needs assessment by the council’s dangerous structures personnel before entry or propping.

JoJo: your cousin is generally right that intact Victorian terraces are robust. But one that has just taken a chimney through its roof is a different situation.

Priya: no, I would not use that pavement. Please keep to the opposite side until the council has assessed it and dealt with the loose material, particularly on the St Dunstan’s school run. The council already knows about the collapse, but its tape covers only No. 43’s front garden, not the footway. Out of hours, dangerous structures is reached through the main council number; please report specifically that the pavement remains open.

Nobody can pronounce Mrs Doherty safe from the pavement. No. 45’s front looks undamaged, and the remaining stack is not over it, but I could not see the 43/45 party wall. It is not my decision, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight; I would encourage her to stay with family until No. 45 has been checked.

For transparency: I’m chartered with IStructE, but this is not a commission, and I have no PI cover for free advice. I’m speaking as a neighbour reporting what was visible from the pavement, nothing more.
